system.summary: Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554: letters plus two series of syllable signs whose vowel is marked by a dot, two dots, a bar, a small o or a p-stroke; groups (cr, pr, tr, qu...), doubles, a nomenclator in Latin letters, and nulls marked by two dots below.

diacritics.note: one dot / two dots / bar / small o / p-stroke select the vowel a / i / e / o / u of a syllable sign

system.notes: Sign names follow targets/gonzaga1549 (same cipher, Brussels chancery hand). The period table AGS MPD D/00203 no. 243 ('Es del año de 1545', issue #618) was used for study only and is not reproduced.

prior_solution.where: Keys (not readings) reconstructed by S. Tomokiyo, cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/spanish2.htm, for the four ciphers covering 18 of the 20 items; the 1544-1554 key after Meister (1906) and Bertomeu Masiá (2009). No printed reading of the letters found.

conditions.human_role: Set the task; Brice Dudout's agents fetched the PARES images on his machine and ran the work; no human transcription.

solution.what: PARES record and image pages for the 20 items: connection reset and HTTP 429 from this machine; no image fetched.

Web search and Tomokiyo's 'Spanish Ciphers during the Reign of Emperor Charles V': 18 of the 20 PARES records are listed there under four ciphers with reconstructed keys (prior_art.tsv); the 2 Nov 2026 vetting had missed it.
Tomokiyo's key images (CharlesV1534.jpg, CharlesV1543.jpg, CharlesV2.jpg, CharlesV3.gif, CharlesV1548.jpg): direct download redirected, images not read.

Review of PR #392: prior_art.tsv compared with the raw HTML of Tomokiyo's spanish2.htm. All 18 PARES numbers, dates, recipients and cipher headings agree; the two 1557 records are absent. The five key images download with a browser user agent and referer (not transcribed). The page source holds Tomokiyo's short trial decipherments of eleven items as HTML comments.
PARES images of 20 records fetched (Spanish exit, earlier sessions); Biblioteca Estense IIIF crops of Campori Lettera K, Karl V sfasc. IV c. 60r/60v for a shape atlas.
Key assembled from Tomokiyo/Masiá and the 1545 AGS table (study only), frozen by SHA-256 before each measurement.

Pre-registered single measurement on 1379,14-18 cipher image 06 (492 tokens, never seen before) against the clear copy of the time: character precision 0.873; 200 within-class value shuffles (letters, syllables, codes, nulls) max 0.477; 200 whole-key shuffles max 0.449; 4.1% signs outside the key. Earlier measurements without the shape atlas: 0.740, 0.783, 0.795 (other portions).

Five 1553 letters (1383,242, 296, 312, 351-353, 364; 20 pages, 12,741 signs) transcribed by shape in two blind passes by separate Claude sub-agents and arbitrated on the image by a third, without values or clear text.

Decode with the frozen key, read by sense under a strict count (sure / probable / supplied / unread): 60-75% of words read per letter, 38-54% sure only; docs/_check_reading.py clean share 0.10-0.38. Phrases such as 'por la via de Leon con cartas de mercaderes', 'la francesa esta en Calvi y la turquesca en Bonifacio', 'la mitad del gasto y la otra mitad le haran ellos' come out, but most sentences keep holes.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The key of the Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554 (published by Tomokiyo after Masiá, completed by the 1545 AGS table) was matched to Figueroa's hand with a shape atlas and validated on a held-out page with a clear copy of the time (0.873). Five 1553 letters decode with the frozen key into Spanish with holes: 60-75% of words read as sense, but holes remain in most sentences at PARES resolution (about 1000 px).

credits.note: Key of the Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554 (after Bertomeu Masiá) and the pointer to the 1545 AGS table; his draft decipherments in the HTML comments of spanish2.htm agree with our openings of 242, 296, 312, 351-353 and 364.
Reconstruction of the Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554 (2009), via Tomokiyo.
gonzaga1549 sign names and the Biblioteca Estense IIIF recipe, used to build the shape atlas.
Pull request: validation and transcriptions made with Claude agents.

gaps.detail: Dots and bars of the syllable signs and several look-alike bases (r-/c-series, me/que) are not separable at PARES resolution; the blind passes agree on 44-80% of signs before arbitration; about 30 recurrent signs have no value in the key. High-resolution AGS reproductions would decide most of them.
Images in hand; not transcribed. 308-311 (duplicate of 16 Sep 1553) and 265-266 would allow collation.
Cipher not identified (Imperial Cipher of 1555, Meister no. 76, or Cg.1 of 1556).

outcome.notes: Status: in progress. Key validated; five 1553 letters transcribed and decoded, not read (holes in most sentences).

texts.label: AGS Estado 242, 1553-05-28
texts.summary: Changes (a cambio), asientos and the Spinola; what remains owed; opening agrees with Tomokiyo's draft.
texts.note: Strict reading count (sure / probable / supplied / unread words, Daniel's 95% rule): 66% of words read as sense, 54% sure only; docs/_check_reading.py clean share 0.375.
